# Afternoon reception findings and next controlled test

2091 distinct CADUs, expected ASM throughout; morning392. Native SatDump logs show repeated deframer sync14:56:10–15:00:00, compared with morning09:46:10–09:46:50. Logs sampled10sec; these are sampled intervals, not claims of uninterrupted lock. Peak demodulator estimate14.36dB vs5.45dB morning. Afternoon image coverage1568x1544 vs1568x304 morning channel1, with edge/missing data artifacts.

Raw-IQ spot checks used64 FFTs of8192 samples each, Hann window, zero-mean samples; mean power in3–65kHz offsets compared with100–220kHz offsets on both sides. This is a comparative band-power metric, NOT calibrated SNR and not a separation of satellite from all interference. Metric13.40dB at14:58:30,8.36dB14:59:30,1.35dB15:00:30. Near-full-scale samples <=0.0001% in inspected windows; no evidence of widespread digital clipping in those windows. This does not rule out analog-stage overload. Signal-band fading is more supported than a display-only lock failure, but physical cause remains unresolved.

Preserved working configuration on Pi: ~/wni-receiver/profiles/meteor-m2-4-successful-20261105.json.137.9MHz72k,1.024MS/s,gain25.4dB,AGCoff,biasoff,USBpoweredLNA,CS8raw+live. Do not attribute improvement solely to LNA: both morning and afternoon used LNA; satellites and pass geometry differed.

Next controlled-test procedure:
1. Keep successful receiver settings initially. Do not raise gain just because lock drops; substantial SNR was achieved with25.4dB.
2. Record to predicted LOS even after NOSYNC, unless user explicitly requests stop. Recovery is possible; preserving the ending allows analysis of missed opportunities.
3. Log exact time and only one change at a time. Compare modest gain changes only with a visible signal, then return to baseline if no benefit. No scheduled automatic gain control exists for this native GUI.
4. Check safely accessible cable/LNA direction and antenna placement; any physical reorientation test should be from an accessible ground location. Record orientation before/after. No roof climbing during reception.
5. Prioritize comparable M2-4 passes for a clean comparison, and compare frame growth/lock duration as well as peak SNR. M2-3 remains a different test rather than an equivalent comparison.
6. Preserve CADUs, native logs, raw IQ and all image products. Always deliver colour and grayscale outputs together. False colour products are channel combinations, not independent captures; more composites do not add missing geography.

Capture stopped at user request around15:02:42PHT. Raw remains on Pi; it is not backed up locally. Images and CADUs are local copies. No new future reception is armed by this reflection.

# Local Meteor reception — 4 November 2026

Actual antenna/RTL-SDR/Pi reception, not an archive/sample replay.

- Native SatDump 1.2.2 ran Meteor M2-x LRPT 72k at 137.900 MHz and 1.024 MS/s,
  with software DC blocking, RS checking, gain 38.6 dB, AGC/bias off.
- Log polling observed both Viterbi and frame synchronization around
  21:17:50–21:18:00 PHT, with intermittent loss of lock afterward.
- Automatic capture stop executed at 21:32 PHT. Saved CADUs: 138,240 bytes,
  or **135 validated 1024-byte frames**. Offline image processing exited 0.
- Visual inspection of raw channel 4 and corrected MCIR shows a **short image
  strip with cloud-like structure and missing data**, not a complete pass image.
  This establishes partial local image reception; regional coverage, calibrated
  quantities, map registration and scientific suitability are not validated.
- `final_images/` contains derived outputs. `capture-result.json`, CADUs and
  processing log were copied directly from the Pi. Multiple generated composites
  represent the same limited capture, not multiple independent observations.
- Full original CS8 IQ remains on the Pi at
  `/home/adriel/wni-receiver/raw/2026-11-04_12-10-32_1024000SPS_137900000Hz.cs8`.
  It has not been copied to the Mac in this handoff.

Pi capture directory:
`/home/adriel/wni-receiver/decoded/2026-11-04_12-09_meteor_m2-x_lrpt_137.9 MHz/`.

## Recovery and improvement assessment

Replayed a 90-second excerpt spanning 21:17:10–21:18:40 PHT from the preserved
CS8 recording on the Pi, with the standard 72k pipeline, 1.024 MS/s, DC blocking
and RS checking. It recovered **239 distinct validated CADUs** versus 135 distinct
CADUs in the original live capture. These are overlapping versions of the same
reception and must not be added as independent frames/observations.

The recovered channel 4 image in `replay-baseline/MSU-MR-4.png` is 1568×336 pixels,
versus 1568×112 for the original. Both remain limited fragments. The replay CADUs
are `replay-baseline.cadu`; the native receiver log is `native-reception.log`.
The original raw IQ remains unchanged on the Pi. The excerpt is stored there at
`~/wni-receiver/tests/recovery-20261104/2026-11-04_13-17-10_1024000SPS_137900000Hz.cs8`.

Two controlled replay trials changed only PLL bandwidth: 0.001 recovered zero
frames; 0.004 recovered 61; standard 0.002 recovered 239. Therefore retain the
standard setting rather than adopting either trial. Results and replay log are
in `replay-baseline/`. Higher replay yield does not by itself prove CPU drops,
and it does not resolve why the received signal was weak/intermittent.

The user clarified that open ground lies beneath the dipole arms and reported
no nearby water tank, railing or wall. Metal-roof interference is not established;
actual antenna height and clearance remain uncertain. Priorities for another
attempt: confirm dipole geometry and clearance, compare manual receiver gains
using valid-frame yield, and verify the existing filtered LNA's power method,
direction and SDR compatibility before a powered-vs-bypass comparison.

policy: Local reception archive only. All displayed captures conservatively classified as partial. Image variants do not represent separate observations. ASM checks confirm framing, not independent RS revalidation. No geographic image overlays until scan timing and georeferencing are validated.
